newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Lonrho profit up, focus on demerger.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Lonrho profit up, focus on demerger.

text.p: Conglomerate Lonrho Plc, which has been working for the last year on splitting itself up, is set to report a modest full-year profit rise on Thursday, analysts said.
But as the company will likely transform itself completely this year after having already made one big investment, analysts believe Thursday's results are largely immaterial.
"We will be getting the results of a company which already ceased to exist in the form it had when its financial year ended," said Charles Kernot at Paribas Capital Markets.
Rather than the results, industry watchers are more keen to hear about progress on the planned sale of the Princess hotels.
Lonrho already sold its Metropole hotel chain to Stakis Plc in October, when it said it expected to conclude a sale of Princess in November. But nothing has materialised so far.
The Princess delay comes as no surprise to analysts who have become used to a string of hold-ups and adjustments of Lonrho's original demerger plan announced in January 1996.
The demerger hitches have hurt Lonrho's shares, which fell a total 28.7 percent last year.
"The delays are unsettling and unnerving the stock market," said Kernot.

The major obstacle currently in the way of Lonrho's demerger is an EU investigation into the competition implications of the 28 percent stake held in the British firm by South Africa's mining group Anglo American.
Anglo and Lonrho both have substantial producers of platinum, which is used in car exhaust catalysts.

Analysts don't expect any statements on the planned break-up of Lonrho's mining and African trading operations until the EU releases its findings. These may only come out in April and may call for the sale of Lonrho's platinum interests.
Meanwhile, forecasts for pre-tax profit for the year to September range between 156 and 166 million stg, up from 151 million the previous year.
Analysts said the profit rise would be mainly due to a strong performance of the hotels business, but would be held back by a higher interesest charge and a poor performance of Ashanti Goldfields.
Lonrho has a 33.6 percent stake in the Ghanaian goldmine, which is suffering from rising costs rather than from falling gold prices.
